Scottish historian and broadcaster Neil Oliver joins Tucker Carlson for a sweeping talk on banks, empires, and modern crises. Oliver argues that banking power quietly took over the fate of nations. The conversation ranges across World War II, Brexit, and COVID from his coastal Scottish view.

Oliver lays out how finance, in his telling, bent empires and governments to its will. He shares his dissenting takes on the war, Britain's exit from Europe, and the pandemic years. Carlson finds a kindred skeptic across the Atlantic. Questioning viewers get a broad, poetic brief against the modern order.
